title: nf-austin/infercnv pipeline parameters
description: Automated InferCNV pipeline with clustering, CIN scoring, and matrix concatenation

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Where the count matrices come from and where results go.

input.description: Samplesheet CSV listing the samples to run.
input.help_text: Columns: `sample` and `h5ad`. One row per sample; `sample` becomes the output subdirectory name and must be unique. Use this rather than `--h5ad_dir` when launching from Seqera Platform. Mutually exclusive with `--h5ad_dir`.

h5ad_dir.description: Ad-hoc alternative to a samplesheet: a glob matching .h5ad files, e.g. 'data/*.h5ad'.
h5ad_dir.help_text: The sample id is taken from each filename with any trailing `_annotated` stripped. Mutually exclusive with `--input`.

outdir.description: Output directory. Use an absolute path on a cluster or on cloud storage.

reference_options.title: Reference options
reference_options.description: Gene-order file InferCNV uses to place genes on chromosomes.

gene_order.help_text: The recommended path on HPC: PREPARE_REFERENCE downloads an Ensembl GTF at runtime, and compute nodes usually have no outbound network. Build it once on a login node and pass the path here.

gtf.description: Pre-downloaded Ensembl GTF (.gtf or .gtf.gz). Skips only the download, still builds the gene-order file.
gtf.help_text: Use when you want the pipeline to build the positions file but cannot reach Ensembl from the compute node.

species.description: Ensembl species name used to auto-download the GTF.
species.help_text: Only used when neither --gene_order nor --gtf is given.

release.description: Ensembl release used to auto-download the GTF.
release.help_text: Only used when neither --gene_order nor --gtf is given.

analysis_options.title: Clustering and InferCNV options
analysis_options.description: How cells are clustered and CNVs called.

resolution.description: Leiden clustering resolution. Higher gives more, smaller clusters.

cutoff.description: InferCNV expression cutoff: minimum mean count per gene across cells.
cutoff.help_text: Upstream recommends 1 for Smart-seq2 and 0.1 for 10x-style droplet data.

container_options.title: Container options
container_options.description: Which images the processes run in.

infercnv_container.description: R/Bioconductor image carrying InferCNV and zellkonverter, used by RUN_INFERCNV.

infercnv_py_container.description: Python/scanpy image used by the clustering, annotation, concat and reference steps.

execution_options.title: Execution environment
execution_options.description: Cluster scheduler, image caches and bind mounts. Relevant when running on HPC.
execution_options.help_text: Use the `slurm` profile together with an engine profile: `-profile slurm,singularity`. On Seqera Platform a SLURM compute environment already sets the executor, so you normally only need the cache and bind settings here.

slurm_queue.help_text: Only used with `-profile slurm`. Left unset, no --partition flag is emitted and the cluster default applies.

cluster_options.description: Raw sbatch options appended to every job, e.g. '--qos=long'.

singularity_cache_dir.description: Shared directory for pulled Singularity images.
singularity_cache_dir.help_text: Put this on shared storage the compute nodes can read. $HOME is quota-limited and is not always mounted on compute nodes. Defaults to NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR, then Nextflow's own $NXF_HOME location.

conda_cache_dir.description: Shared directory for created conda environments.

singularity_bind.description: Extra paths to bind into the container, comma-separated, e.g. '/mnt/gpfs,/scratch'.
singularity_bind.help_text: autoMounts only binds paths Nextflow itself resolved. HPC filesystems are routinely symlinked (/data -> /mnt/gpfs/...), which shows up as 'file not found' inside the container even though the host path exists. Bind the real parent here.

max_job_request_options.title: Maximum job request options
max_job_request_options.help_text: RUN_INFERCNV requests 16 CPUs by default. On a small machine lower `--max_cpus`, or the task cannot be submitted at all.

max_cpus.description: Maximum CPUs for any single job.

max_memory.description: Maximum memory for any single job.

max_time.description: Maximum time for any single job.

help.description: Print the help message and exit.
